notes: Measured by the playtest lane on 2026-09-22: 27 day-pressed sessions won with 81%; zero sessions lost with about 41%. The rival's weekly cadence gives it roughly a twenty-eighth of the player's action budget.

Evidence from ChatGPT's federal winner-share memo, 2026-09-22 (docs/research/chatgpt-answers/2026-09-22-nationwide-2340/Our-Civic-Duty--federal-winner-shares-and-campaign-effort-evidence--2026-09-22.md (Drive 1V-IU6Ng8bwi2fOTrh2S6APrmAdImxiUs, SHA-256 de9c6e20d0813a28b2b65865647a3f69b614ef96661a59202546f55840f6b70a)): Kalla and Broockman 2018 (49 field experiments) find an average persuasion effect of zero on vote choice in general elections, with early effects decaying by election day; Baum and Owens 2023 (Tennessee House District 37) find a candidate's own door-knocking gave +3 points of vote and +6 of margin; Gerber and Green 2000 (New Haven) find canvassing raised turnout only. The evidence does not support a fixed 1.35-point gain per 90-minute shift compounded over weeks. lamontae decided reach is finite and repetition has diminishing returns; the reach, the rate and the ceiling are UNKNOWN pending calibration, which is what this question still asks for.

lamontae, 2026-09-22 8:08 p.m. Eastern: door-knocking does have returns, and they should vary with who is knocking. An unknown candidate out of state, like Jimmy Carter starting in New Hampshire, gets very little return. A sitting president, someone the voter already knows, or an already popular candidate may get more, and the effect may last longer; a campaign can also snowball. The answer should say how name recognition, prior contact and popularity change the size and duration of a contact's effect.
question: In a real state legislative or local race, how much does a candidate's own effort (door-knocking hours, volunteers, fundraising, paid advertising) move vote share, how much can a candidate realistically raise per session of call time at each level of office, and how active is a typical opponent over a campaign?

Both give the model's shape and say no coefficients were supplied.

title: How much a canvassing shift, a dollar or a week of an opponent's work actually moves a local or legislative race
usableAnswer: Published estimates (field experiments, campaign-finance data) for: vote-share effect of canvassing contact per hour or per contact, with diminishing returns; fundraising per hour of call time or typical totals by office level (the FEC corpus the game already holds may answer the federal end); effect of advertising spend at local and state level; and how many weeks and what kinds of activity a typical challenger and incumbent run. Ranges are fine; say which are well established and which are thin.
whyItMatters:
The owner said on 2026-09-22 that a race has to be an actual race: 'you need to be going against people. You can't win every time.' The effort arithmetic is why the player nearly always wins, and none of it is sourced. At main 9f42ba19:

1. src/simulation/campaigns.ts:1055-1059 — a 90-minute field shift gains minutes x workers x 3/2 x a 60-140% swing, 81-189 basis points each; ads gain spend in cents / 500.
2. src/presentation/campaign-projection.ts:63, :220, :223 — sessions of 90 minutes, back to back until 9 p.m., with no daily cap and no diminishing returns, so about four a day.
3. src/simulation/campaign-opponents.ts:88-104 and :874 — the opponent acts once every 7 days, starts with $0, raises $600-2,500 a week; 'Authored game defaults; not empirical', no question named.
4. src/simulation/campaigns.ts:1209 — the player raises $850-1,750 per session whether the race is for a town council or governor.
5. src/simulation/campaigns.ts:379-381 — starting support 850 + 0..300 per candidate, minus 60 for the player.

The answered questions how-an-election-night-should-come-out and proposed-balance-parameters-nobody-confirmed (A09) say how the outcome should be modeled but explicitly supply 'no newly researched empirical turnout/persuasion coefficients'. The field size is covered by state-legislative-seat-calendar-and-field; this question is only the magnitudes.
